column3: The Hebrew says “all the people of war” and commands Joshua to rise and go up; BSB has “the whole army” and supplies an explicit command to “attack” Ai.
The Hebrew refers to Ai’s spoil and livestock with singular feminine suffixes; BSB uses plural “their.”
The Hebrew says the people rose to go up to Ai; BSB says the army “set out to attack” it.
The Hebrew explicitly names the city three times; BSB names it once and uses “it” for the distance clause.
The Hebrew calls those with Joshua “the people”; BSB says “the troops.”
The Hebrew uses “they” in the enemy’s quotation and ends with “we will flee”; BSB supplies “The Israelites” and makes the final flight an “as” clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the city” and says “according to the word of the LORD”; BSB uses “it” and “as the LORD has commanded.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the people” and says “in the morning”; BSB has “his men,” then “them,” and supplies “next.”
The Hebrew says the valley was between singular “him” and Ai; BSB uses plural “them” and “the city.”
The Hebrew begins with an unnamed “he”; BSB explicitly names Joshua.
The Hebrew actively says the people positioned the camp and rear force; BSB uses the passive “the forces were stationed.”

The Hebrew does not explicitly name what the king saw and then uses plural verbs for hurrying, rising early, and going out; BSB supplies “the Israelites” and makes the king the singular subject of hurrying out.
The Hebrew uses a passive form for being struck before the enemy; BSB says they “let themselves be beaten back.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew joins Ai and Bethel with “and”; BSB has “or.”
The Hebrew twice names the lance “in” Joshua’s hand and ends with “the city”; BSB calls it “your” or “his” lance and repeats “Ai.”
The Hebrew explicitly says Joshua stretched out his hand; BSB refers to this with “he did so.”
The Hebrew uses the image of having no “hands” to flee and says the fleeing people turned toward the pursuer; BSB has “could not escape” and “became the pursuers.”
The Hebrew repeats “the city” in “the smoke of the city”; BSB uses “it.”
The Hebrew begins with “these” and leaves the subjects of being surrounded and striking unnamed; BSB explicitly names the ambush, the men of Ai, and Israel.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew twice uses “the mouth of the sword”; BSB has “fallen by the sword” and “put it to the sword.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says Joshua stretched out his hand with the lance; BSB describes the hand as holding the lance.
The Hebrew has “according to the word of the LORD, which He commanded”; BSB combines this as “as the LORD had commanded.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately says Joshua commanded and that they brought the body down and threw it; BSB makes those actions the content of his command.
Close to the Hebrew.
